path_rules.description: At startup FS_InitFilesystemEx mounts the base game directories in this order: id1/ (or ID1/ on case-sensitive filesystems where the directory is upper-case), then ezquake/, then qw/, then (if set) the user's home directory. Each is pushed onto fs_searchpaths via FS_AddGameDirectory, which pushes to the head of the list — so the effective lookup order is homedir > qw > ezquake > id1.

fs_searchpaths is a singly-linked list traversed head-first. Every FS_AddPathHandle call sets search->next = fs_searchpaths then fs_searchpaths = search, so the most recently added directory or archive is checked first. Lookups (FS_FLocateFile) walk the list from head to tail and return the first match.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddPathHandle(char * probablepath, searchpathfuncs_t * funcs, void * handle, qbool copyprotect, qbool istemporary, FS_Load_File_Types loadstuff)

path_rules.description: Within a game directory FS_AddDataFiles loads pak0.<ext>, pak1.<ext>, pak2.<ext>, ... in numeric-ascending order until one is missing. Because each is pushed to the head of fs_searchpaths on load, higher-numbered paks end up earlier in lookup order. Effect: pakN.pak overrides pak(N-1).pak for same-name entries.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddDataFiles(char * pathto, searchpath_t * parent, char * extension, searchpathfuncs_t * funcs)

path_rules.description: FS_AddPathHandle loads archives in this order per directory: FS_LOAD_FILE_PAK (.pak), then FS_LOAD_FILE_PK3 (.pk3), then FS_LOAD_FILE_PK4 (.pk4). Later-loaded kinds sit higher on the LIFO stack, so precedence is: pk4 > pk3 > pak. QuakeWorld installs rarely use pk4; in practice this collapses to pk3 > pak.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddPathHandle(char * probablepath, searchpathfuncs_t * funcs, void * handle, qbool copyprotect, qbool istemporary, FS_Load_File_Types loadstuff)

path_rules.description: After loading pakN.<ext>, pakN+1.<ext>, ... in order, FS_AddDataFiles enumerates `*.<ext>` in the same directory via FS_AddWildDataFiles. Wildcard-discovered archives are pushed after the numbered ones, so they sit higher on the stack and take precedence over numbered paks of the same extension.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddDataFiles(char * pathto, searchpath_t * parent, char * extension, searchpathfuncs_t * funcs)

path_rules.description: FS_AddGameDirectory pushes the directory itself onto fs_searchpaths (via FS_AddPathHandle), THEN FS_AddPathHandle triggers FS_AddDataFiles which pushes the directory's archives on top. Net effect: archives override loose files in the same directory.

If a file named `pak.lst` exists in the game directory, FS_AddDataFiles skips the `*.<ext>` wildcard enumeration entirely. Only explicitly listed paks (via pak0..pakN numbered loop) load, giving the user a way to constrain which archives mount.
path_rules.verified_function_fingerprint: FS_AddDataFiles(char * pathto, searchpath_t * parent, char * extension, searchpathfuncs_t * funcs)

path_rules.description: FS_SetGamedir frees every searchpath entry above fs_base_searchpaths (the stack snapshot taken after id1/ezquake/qw/homedir load at init) before mounting the new mod dir. This means a gamedir switch does NOT keep the previous mod's entries — only the base stack survives. Each `gamedir` command thus swaps mods cleanly.

After unwinding, FS_SetGamedir calls FS_AddGameDirectory for the new mod and, if set, FS_AddHomeDirectory for homedir/<mod>. The mod directory sits on top of the base stack (qw/ezquake/id1), so assets missing from the mod fall through to qw/, then ezquake/, then id1/.

`-basedir <path>` overrides the auto-detected com_basedir (the directory above id1/, ezquake/, qw/). Checked before Sys_getcwd fallback; when present, id1/ezquake/qw are resolved relative to this value.
`-nohome` clears com_homedir so no ~/ezQuake (Windows) or ~/.ezquake (POSIX) directory is mounted. Without it, the home directory is always added after qw/ at startup.

`-data <subdir>` can be repeated to mount additional game directories under com_basedir, applied as extra FS_AddGameDirectory calls after id1/ezquake/qw. Each -data entry pushes on top of the previous one.

`-userdir <dir> <type>` sets a user-specific media directory via FS_SetUserDirectory, separating user-generated files (screenshots, demos, configs) from the base install. Applied after base stack but before any gamedir switch.
`-game <mod>` (or `+gamedir <mod>`) calls FS_SetGamedir at startup, mounting <mod> on top of the base stack. Equivalent to running `gamedir <mod>` at the console immediately after init.
